gloss: magic trick; conjuring; sleight of hand

definitions.gloss: magic trick; conjuring; sleight of hand; stage magic
definitions.explanation: The art or performance of stage magic — making objects appear, disappear, or transform in ways that seem impossible. A somewhat formal or old-fashioned word compared to the common loanword マジック.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{得意|とくい}な{奇術|きじゅつ}で{子供|こども}たちを{喜|よろこ}ばせた。
examples.english: My grandfather delighted the children with his specialty magic trick.

examples.japanese: {奇術|きじゅつ}{師|し}は{観客|かんきゃく}の{目|め}の{前|まえ}でコインを{消|け}してみせた。
examples.english: The magician made a coin vanish right before the audience's eyes.

examples.japanese: {伝統|でんとう}{的|てき}な{日本|にほん}の{奇術|きじゅつ}は、{和傘|わがさ}や{扇子|せんす}などの{道具|どうぐ}を{巧|たく}みに{使|つか}う。
examples.english: Traditional Japanese magic skillfully uses tools such as paper umbrellas and folding fans.

notes:
Composed of {奇|き} (strange, marvelous, curious) and {術|じゅつ} (art, technique, skill). Refers to the art of performing illusions — card tricks, coin tricks, vanishing acts, and stage magic more broadly.

REGISTER: Somewhat formal or old-fashioned. In everyday conversation, the loanword マジック or {手品|てじな} is far more common. {奇術|きじゅつ} is still used in literary contexts, for traditional Japanese stage magic, and in the word {奇術|きじゅつ}{師|し} (professional magician).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {奇術|きじゅつ}を{行|おこな}う: to perform a magic trick (formal)
- {奇術|きじゅつ}{師|し}: a magician, conjurer
- {奇術|きじゅつ}ショー: a magic show
- {奇術|きじゅつ}の{腕|うで}: skill at magic

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手品|てじな}: magic trick, sleight of hand — the everyday native word; most common in casual speech
- マジック: magic — the common English loanword; used for card magic, stage shows, and modern entertainment
- {魔術|まじゅつ}: magic, sorcery — refers to supposed real magic or witchcraft, not stage tricks
- {幻術|げんじゅつ}: illusion, sorcery — more literary; used for supernatural illusions in fiction
